summary: Attacked the extraction of Bennett-Siksek, 'A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums' (Annals 191 (2020), 355-392, including the Granville addendum in section 12) — 152 items, 12 routes including one new roadmap and two Part IIs. Two findings, both low: the record carries no sourceIssues although the published paper doubles a verb in the proof of Lemma 4.1, and its own routeAudit says 130 missing items where there are 129. Everything structural held. The source hash reproduces; all 33 cited declarations exist at the pin and all 16 planned stage references resolve; all 129 missing items are routed exactly once; both Part II titles are exact prefix extensions with free ids and the new roadmap id is free; the paper's numbered statements are fully covered, the two apparent gaps being citations to other works; and no other extraction proposes any of the three roadmaps.
checked: The source itself, re-fetched from the Annals URL the record gives and hashed: SHA-256 3920a7524a37870942fe3591ac858db23cb604f4331bccd2a6dc5f11a1671fbf, matching the recorded hash exactly, 39 pages. The PDF is not stamped, so the hash reproducing means the same document was read.

Every declaration the items cite, at the pinned commits: 33 references, all present. Every stage reference of the 12 planned items: 16 references, all resolving to real atlas stages, including the four Tau Ceti ModularForms and EllipticCurves layers and the campaign stages R01.6, R19.1, R19.6, RP.4, DWP.1, BSD.0, CM.3, AN.2 and R29.6.

Routing, in full: 129 missing items, 129 distinct routed ids, 129 route slots, so every missing item is routed exactly once, nothing not missing is routed, and no route's `items` array repeats an id. This is what produced finding 2, since the record's own routeAudit says 130.

The two Part II proposals against section 15. 'Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: effective residual comparisons' is an exact prefix extension of its parent's atlas title, and so is 'Elliptic curves, Part II: Legendre models, descent and character interfaces'; both roadmap ids are free, as is the new roadmap id ErdosProgressionPowers, which carries a title, an area and a substantive brief.

Whether section 16 requires an API and unit tests on a paper item, since 26 of the missing items are definitions or constructions and none carries either. It does not: section 16's item schema is id, kind, name, statement, locator, status, library, planned and note, and none of its rules asks for an API or tests, which belong to blueprint nodes under sections 3-4 and 12. The absence is correct, not a defect.

Coverage of the paper's numbered statements. Of the 42 numbered labels the text mentions, 40 are carried by an item. The two that are not are references to other papers rather than statements of this one: 'a version of which first appeared in the proof of Theorem 1.5 of [1]' and 'From Proposition 5.25 of [19]'. Coverage is complete.

The paper itself for mistakes, as a test of the empty sourceIssues. Internal cross-references are consistent: every in-paper numbered statement that is referenced is declared. Repeated-word scanning finds 'log log' 16 times, which is the iterated logarithm, and one genuine doubling, which is finding 1.

Competing proposals for the three roadmaps this extraction introduces: none. ErdosProgressionPowers, EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons and EllipticLegendreCharacterInterfaces are each proposed by this extraction alone, so no coalescence is owed and nothing is planned twice.

findings.claim: The extraction records no mistakes in the source, but the published paper contains a misprint that section 18 exists to record: in the proof of Lemma 4.1 the verb is doubled, 'If instead p divides divides precisely two terms'. The extraction says it read the entire published paper, so this is an omission rather than a limit of scope. It affects nothing — the intended reading is fixed by the parallel sentence three lines earlier — but an unrecorded misprint is one the errata register will not carry.
findings.evidence: The source block records the published Annals PDF at https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v191-n2-p02-s.pdf with SHA-256 3920a7524a37870942fe3591ac858db23cb604f4331bccd2a6dc5f11a1671fbf and says 'Entire published paper read; sensitive displays also inspected as page images.' I re-fetched that PDF on 24 September 2026 and the hash reproduces exactly, so the file is not stamped and we are reading the same 39-page document. On PDF page 10, whose running head is the printed page number 364, the proof of Lemma 4.1 reads: 'Suppose first that p divides precisely one such term, say p | n + id. ... If instead p divides divides precisely two terms, say p | n + id and p | n + (i + p)d, then we choose ...'. The doubling is in the published text, not an artefact of the text layer: the surrounding sentence is otherwise clean and the first clause of the same proof has the single verb. A scan of the whole paper for repeated words finds exactly one other pattern, 'log log', which occurs 16 times and is the iterated logarithm rather than a doubling. The paper is otherwise clean on the checks I ran: every one of its 34 numbered statements that is referenced internally is declared, and the two labels that appear without a matching declaration, Theorem 1.5 and Proposition 5.25, are citations to other works ('a version of which first appeared in the proof of Theorem 1.5 of [1]' and 'From Proposition 5.25 of [19]').
findings.fix: Add one entry to `sourceIssues` in the section 18 shape, with kind 'misprint', locator 'proof of Lemma 4.1, printed p. 364 (PDF p. 10)', printed 'If instead p divides divides precisely two terms, say p | n + id and p | n + (i + p)d', correction 'If instead p divides precisely two terms, say p | n + id and p | n + (i + p)d', reason 'The verb is doubled; the parallel clause three lines earlier reads "Suppose first that p divides precisely one such term"', and affects 'nothing'. The `known` and `searched` fields need the fixer's own check for a published erratum or corrigendum to this Annals paper before they are filled in; I did not search for one, so I do not assert that none exists.

findings.claim: The extraction's own verification miscounts its missing items. `routeAudit` opens 'All 130 missing items routed once'; the record has 129 missing items. The routing itself is correct — all 129 are routed, each exactly once — so only the self-report is wrong, but it is the sentence a reviewer checks the routing against.
findings.evidence: The `items` array holds 152 items with statuses 129 missing, 12 planned and 11 library. Collecting the ids named by the twelve routes gives 129 distinct ids and 129 route slots in total, so every missing item is routed exactly once, no item is routed twice, no non-missing item is routed, and no route repeats an id inside its own `items` array. Against that, verification.routeAudit reads 'All 130 missing items routed once.'
findings.fix: Change '130' to '129' in verification.routeAudit. Nothing else needs to move: the routing the sentence describes is correct as it stands.
